## Day 1 — Evaluating community information

# Day 1 — Term 1, Week 1, Day 1 — Copper Worksheet

**Learner name:** ____________________________________  **School:** __________________________

**Class/Form:** Form 2  **Subject:** English  **Date:** __________________  **Term/Week/Day:** 1/1/1

**Ability pathway:** Copper  **Teacher:** __________________________

**PacEdu status:** ORIGINAL PRACTICE DRAFT — PENDING_TEACHER_REVIEW — PENDING_OFFICIAL_INDICATOR_VERIFICATION.

**Accessible response:** You may write, type, use Braille, dictate, sign, use AAC, point to choices or use another agreed method. Ask for large print, audio or repeated instructions if needed.

## Today's learning goal
The learner will identify the central idea and select accurate details that support it in the context of **Evaluating community information**.

## Read this complete passage

### The Notice on the Board

A notice on a community board announces a meeting about water supply. It includes a date, venue, organiser and contact details. A second copy shared online leaves out the date and adds an unverified claim. Students compare both versions and discuss why readers should check the complete notice before acting.

**Word help:** reliable; omission; verify. Ask for a spoken, signed, pictured or translated explanation where needed.

## Worked example
The central idea is the main message; a supporting detail is a specific fact that helps explain it.

**Model response:** The main idea is that evaluating community information. I support this by selecting a detail stated in the passage.

## Today's learning goal
The learner will create a coherent response using details from the text and language suited to an audience and purpose in the context of **Evaluating community information**.

## Read this complete passage

### The Notice on the Board

A notice on a community board announces a meeting about water supply. It includes a date, venue, organiser and contact details. A second copy shared online leaves out the date and adds an unverified claim. Students compare both versions and discuss why readers should check the complete notice before acting.

**Word help:** reliable; omission; verify. Ask for a spoken, signed, pictured or translated explanation where needed.

## Worked example
Plan the audience and purpose first, select relevant details, then organise ideas into a clear beginning, middle and end.

**Model response:** My response will name its audience and purpose, use two relevant details, and follow a clear structure.

## Today's learning goal
The learner will identify the central idea and select accurate details that support it in the context of **Restoring a coastal habitat**.

## Read this complete passage

### A Mangrove Recovery Plan

A coastal group maps damaged mangrove areas before planning restoration. They consult local knowledge, check tide conditions and select suitable native species with expert advice. Planting is only one part of the plan: rubbish control, monitoring and protection from trampling are also needed. The group sets review dates to measure survival.

**Word help:** restoration; native; monitor. Ask for a spoken, signed, pictured or translated explanation where needed.

## Worked example
The central idea is the main message; a supporting detail is a specific fact that helps explain it.

**Model response:** The main idea is that restoring a coastal habitat. I support this by selecting a detail stated in the passage.

## Read this complete passage

**Word help:** variable; limitation; conclusion. Ask for a spoken, signed, pictured or translated explanation where needed.

## Today's learning goal
The learner will identify the central idea and select accurate details that support it in the context of **Cultural expression and respect**.

## Read this complete passage

### Who Tells the Story?

Students prepare a performance based on a community story. Before adapting it, they ask who has permission to share it and whether any parts should remain private. They credit contributors and explain the choices made in the programme note. The class discusses the relationship between creativity and responsibility.
